marta (AE): Quick sync — big enterprise (regulated infra) wants an on-prem, fully air-gapped POC. They asked about packaging, upgrade cadence, and what we charge for offline bundles/shipping. Looping @drew (SE) and @rachel for pricing.

drew (SE): Ok. Two quick clarifying q's for the customer: 1) Can they accept physical media (encrypted USB or external SSD via courier)? 2) Are they ok with a jumpbox (air-gapped) that we provide a signed bundle to, or must everything be zero-touch on their side?

lee (Customer-CTO): We can accept couriered encrypted SSDs. We cannot do any outbound network egress from the cluster. Jumpbox is fine but must live inside their DMZ (no internet).

rachel (Sales): Noted. Pricing: for a standard POC we usually include one minibundle + staging support. Extra bundles or custom signing key options are add-ons. @marta do they need dedicated engineer onsite?

marta (AE): They might — they asked about a 2-week onboarding window and troubleshooting. Could become an SOW item.

drew (SE): Packaging suggestion: use delta minibundles (binary diffs) to minimize media size and transfer time. We can chunk into <=2GB files, include a signed manifest, and a verification script. Example manifest snippet:

```
name: redwood_onprem_v1.3.2
chunks:
  - id: chunk-0001
    size: 1.8GB
    sha256: 3b7a...f9c1
  - id: chunk-0002
    size: 450MB
    sha256: a1d2...c4e3
signature: MEUCIQCy... (notary-v2)
```

Verification CLI (run on jumpbox):

```
redwood-verify --manifest manifest.yaml --cert vendor-notary.pub
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "manifest validation failed"; exit 1; fi
```

This approach lets us send multiple small deltas instead of a huge monolith.

lee (Customer-CTO): How do we handle emergency CVE patches? Our security team mandates a max exposure window of 30 days for critical CVEs.

drew (SE): We support hotfix-only bundles: signed, minimal runtime patches that apply in-place. Delivery options: same courier flow or, if they allow a sealed one-way USB path, we can provision a release via jumpbox staging area. Docs/showback in runbook: offline-hotfix.md + checklist.

rachel (Sales): Commercials: POC baseline (1 minibundle + remote support) = $Xk. Onsite engineer or accelerated hotfix SLA = additional retainer. Physical shipping/handling billed per-shipment. We can add a war-room SOW line for 30-day patch coverage during POC.

lee (Customer-CTO): They want to avoid vendor-managed keys. Can we support customer-supplied signing keys (they hold private key)?

drew (SE): Yes — we can support customer key import into our signing tool so they sign the manifest locally before couriering. We will need an agreed process for key escrow instructions and verification steps. That will be slightly more manual and adds to lead time.

marta (AE): Action items: 1) @drew to draft packaging/runbook + verification script. 2) @rachel to propose POC pricing with two variants (remote support vs onsite + hotfix retainer). 3) @lee to share security questionnaire answers re: key custody and courier policy.

ops-bot: Created POC ticket #POC-6221 and attached basic deliverables checklist. Assigned to drew. ETA initial bundle draft: +3 business days.

drew (SE): I'll post the initial bundle spec + sample manifest in the ticket. Also: fallback strategy for air-gapped — since they can't fallback to hosted models, include a small onboard model variant (e.g., quantized 4GB runtime) in the base bundle as a safe-mode. If a heavy model fails, app falls back to the onboard variant.

lee (Customer-CTO): Good. Please include verification steps and rollback steps in the runbook. Security team will review.

marta (AE): Great — I'll set a follow-up call after Drew posts the docs. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
